issue.title: lastcall: {count} {noun} for {project} (audit of {sha})
issue.intro: Valid findings that lastcall did not turn into a pull request: they need your decision, or they are too large for one. Close this issue when you have decided.
plan.title: lastcall: {count} {noun} for {project} (improvement plan at {sha})
plan.intro: Improvements that lastcall checked against the code. Tick the ones you want: lastcall builds each one as a pull request, verified by your tests, in its next run on this project. Close this issue when you are done with it: the ideas you did not tick are dropped.
pr.footer: lastcall: audit of `{sha}` with {engine}; findings {ids}; implemented with {model} ({effort}); {checked}; secret scan: clean.
pr.idea.footer: lastcall: idea {ids} of the improvement plan {plan}; implemented with {model} ({effort}); {checked}; secret scan: clean.
pr.conflict: This pull request no longer merges cleanly into {branch}. lastcall closed it: what it changed goes back to pending, and a later run makes the change again on the current code.
revert.title: Revert "{title}"
revert.body: lastcall watched {url} after its merge, and {reason}. This pull request reverts {sha}. Merge it if that change is the cause, or close it if it is not. lastcall paused the project: activate it again on the Projects page.
watch.checks: the checks of the merged commit failed ({names}), where they passed before it
watch.health: {address} stopped answering ({count} checks in a row)
pr.ticket.footer: Fixes #{number}. lastcall: issue #{number}, labelled `lastcall`; implemented with {model} ({effort}); {checked}; secret scan: clean.
pr.tests.footer: lastcall: tests for `{sha}` with {engine}; findings {ids}; written with {model} ({effort}); {checked}; they change only tests; secret scan: clean.
pr.deps.footer: lastcall: dependency upgrades for `{sha}` with {engine}; findings {ids}; made with {model} ({effort}); {checked}; secret scan: clean.
ticket.stuck:
lastcall worked on this issue and stopped: {why}

Once the issue says what was missing, add the label `lastcall` again.
ticket.red: its change did not pass the project's checks, twice.
ticket.secrets: the secret scan stopped its change.

web.runs.fanout: When several accounts burst at the same time, they review the same project together, and one judge keeps what holds.
web.runs.fanout_hint: Each account's reviewers spend that account's quota; the judge and the fixes spend the quota of the one with the most left. A subscription bursts only in the two days before its reset, so two that reset on different days rarely meet. To combine your accounts at any time, choose “All free accounts, one judge” in the Account field of the “Run now” group of a project on the Projects page, then press “Audit now”.
web.signals.title: Errors in production
web.signals.intro: lastcall can read the errors your apps send to Sentry or GlitchTip. Only the error's type, its masked message and the lines of your code reach the models: never variables, requests or user data.
web.signals.step1: Create a token that can only read: Project › Read and Issue & Event › Read (project:read and event:read). In GlitchTip: your profile › Auth Tokens. In Sentry:
web.signals.step2: Give lastcall the tracker's address, the organization and the token below. lastcall reads one error to check them, and saves them only if that works.
web.signals.step3: On the Projects page, give each project the name of its project in the tracker, as its URLs write it.
web.signals.url_hint: https://sentry.io, or the address of your GlitchTip or of your own Sentry.
web.signals.org_hint: Its slug, as in the tracker's URLs: /organizations/acme/ is acme.
web.signals.token_hint: lastcall keeps it in its secret store and never shows it again.
web.signals.token_keep: Empty: lastcall keeps the one it has.
web.signals.bad: Give an address (http or https), the organization's slug and the token.
web.signals.control: The token cannot hold line breaks or other control characters: paste it again, on one line.
web.signals.failed: The tracker did not answer as expected: {error}
web.logs.title: Container logs
web.logs.intro: If your apps run in Docker on this same machine, lastcall can read their containers' logs, with no change to your apps: the errors, grouped by kind, and the restarts.
web.logs.step1: lastcall suggests a project for each container from its image (ghcr.io/owner/name), its Compose project or its name. It reads none until you choose it: tick the suggestions to read them, or type a project next to any other container.
web.logs.step2: lastcall then reads the last 24 hours of those containers, every 30 minutes and before each run: only their logs and state, never anything else of them.
web.logs.none: No containers on this machine besides lastcall's own.
web.logs.unavailable: The containers can be listed only when lastcall runs with docker compose.
web.logs.failed: The containers could not be listed: {error}
web.logs.label_unknown: Its label names {project}, which is not a project: add it on the Projects page and it is read.
web.logs.others_hint: Type a project next to each one that you want read, then save.
web.logs.not_a_project: “{project}” is not one of your projects. Pick one from the list that opens as you type: the name is the one the Projects page writes.
web.logs.label_title: Or with a label in the compose file
web.logs.label_how: Both ways work together. A container with the label lastcall.project is read for that project with nothing to choose: this page shows it under “Read now”, and its label decides. Add it to the app's compose file, with the project's name as the Projects page writes it, and run docker compose up -d for that app:
web.loki.title: Logs in Loki
web.loki.intro: If your apps run on other machines and Grafana Loki already collects their logs, lastcall can read them there, with nothing to install on those machines.
web.loki.step1: Give Loki's address, one that lastcall can reach, such as http://192.168.1.20:3100, or https://logs-prod-012.grafana.net in Grafana Cloud. lastcall reads it once to check it, and saves it only if that works.
web.loki.step2: If Loki asks for a login, give its user and a token that can only read. In Grafana Cloud, the user is the number in your Loki's details, and the token needs the logs:read scope. A Loki with no login needs neither.
web.loki.step3: Choose the sources to read. lastcall suggests a project from a source's name or its Compose project, and reads nothing until you choose.
web.loki.user_hint: Only for a Loki with a login.
web.loki.token_hint: Only for a Loki with a login. Without a user, it goes as a bearer token.
web.loki.token_keep: Leave it empty to keep the saved one.
web.loki.tenant_hint: Only for a Loki with more than one tenant: its X-Scope-OrgID.
web.loki.bad: Check the fields: the address takes http or https, with no user or query in it, and the user cannot hold a colon.
web.loki.control: The user and the token cannot hold line breaks or other control characters: paste them again, on one line.
web.loki.sources_failed: The sources could not be listed: {error}
web.loki.label: Sources named by the label
web.loki.label_hint: lastcall uses container, container_name, service_name, app or job, the first of them that Loki has. Choose another label if your sources go by it: your choices then start again.
web.loki.no_label: Loki's streams have none of the labels that usually name a source. Choose the one that names yours.
web.loki.none: Loki saw no streams with this label in the last 7 days.
web.tiers.title: Models and effort
web.tiers.intro: Each step of a run asks for a level: fast, balanced or deep. Here you choose the model and the effort of each level for this account. More effort finds more, and spends more of the quota or the budget.
web.tiers.fast_hint: Only your repository's own reviewers that ask for it. No built-in step uses it.
web.tiers.balanced_hint: The reviewers: bugs, security, hygiene, performance, tests and dependencies.
web.tiers.deep_hint: The judge, the implementer that writes each fix, and the improvement plans.
web.tiers.default_hint: An empty model, or Default, keeps lastcall's choice, shown in grey; lastcall updates it as the catalogs change.
web.tiers.keyed_hint: OpenCode passes the effort as the model's variant: choose one that your model offers, or keep Default.
web.tiers.need_models: Give a model for each level: an account on an API key or a local model has no default.

web.help.common.burst: A burst is a run that lastcall starts on its own to use quota you would otherwise lose. On a subscription it starts before the weekly window resets, never more than 48 hours before, just early enough to spend what is left above your reserve, and only if more than 2% is left. An account on an API key bursts at the pace of its monthly budget or at the hours of its schedule; a local model, at the hours of its schedule.
web.help.common.window_throttle: This window only sets the pace. When it reaches 90%, the next step waits for it to reset and then carries on, so a full bar here is not an alarm. It never decides whether lastcall spends.
web.help.common.window_expiring: What this window has left is lost at its reset, so lastcall spends it in a burst before then. It stops when the window reaches your reserve, which stays for you. A high bar just before the reset is lastcall doing its job.
web.help.common.window_model: Some plans also limit one model on its own, such as Claude's weekly window for Opus. Only steps on that model count against it. The Deep level uses Opus by default, so while this window is at your reserve the audit cannot run and no burst starts, even if the account's own week has room.
web.help.common.budget: What this account's steps have cost this calendar month (UTC), as lastcall adds up the cost each step reports. lastcall spreads the budget over the month: behind the calendar means less of the budget is spent than of the month has gone, so it spends now; ahead of it, lastcall waits for the month to catch up.
web.help.common.reserve: The share of each window that expires (the weekly one, on a subscription) that lastcall never spends, so you can still use your subscription yourself. lastcall checks it before every step: with 10, it stops at 90% used, even in the middle of a run. From 0 to 90.
web.help.common.paid: Your provider bills usage beyond the plan on this account: extra usage, credits or overage. So that lastcall never costs you money, it starts no step on this account while that is on. Turn it off at the provider to use the account again.
web.help.common.engine: The program lastcall runs, in its sandbox, for this account's steps. Claude Code and Codex sign in with your subscription. OpenCode runs the models of an API key or of a model server on this machine, and needs no sign-in.
web.help.common.read: The service reads the quota of every enabled account by itself every 15 minutes, without calling any model, so it costs nothing. When this reading is much older, the bars above are out of date: check that the service works.
web.help.common.reviewing: This account is helping another account's audit: its reviewers look for problems and spend this account's quota. The other account is the judge: it decides which findings hold and writes the fixes.
web.help.common.schedule: A schedule is a cron expression with five fields: minute, hour, day of the month, month and weekday, always in UTC, not your local time. * 1-6 * * * means every night from 01:00 to 06:59 UTC. lastcall uses it only when “When it spends” is set to the schedule; with any other choice, saving the account empties it.
web.help.common.findings: Findings are problems an audit found. Pending: confirmed, not in a pull request yet. In review: in an open lastcall pull request; then merged or rejected when you merge or close it, and reverted if its revert was merged. To decide: waiting for your answer in the run's issue; then resolved or dismissed by how you close it. Discarded: the judge did not keep it.
web.help.common.judge: The judge is the last step of an audit. It checks every reviewer's finding against the code and decides what becomes a pull request, what needs your decision and what is dropped. Only audits are shared between accounts: tests, upgrades, ideas and labelled issues always run on one account.
web.help.common.terminal: Type it in a terminal on the machine that hosts lastcall, inside the lastcall folder: the one with compose.yaml.
web.help.dashboard.pause: Pause stops only the bursts, the runs lastcall starts on its own. A run in progress finishes, and the runs you start from the Projects page still start. Resume lets bursts start again.
web.help.dashboard.service: The service is the part of lastcall that works in the background, in the same container as this page. Every minute it checks what to do: it reads quotas every 15 minutes and your pull requests every 10, and it starts the bursts. When it stops, this page keeps working but shows only what it last saw. Restarting the container starts it again, and its log says why it stopped.
web.help.dashboard.prs: Pull requests that lastcall opened and that are still open. While a project has 2 of them, bursts skip it, so reviewing them keeps lastcall working there. Merge or close them on GitHub: lastcall reads what you did every 10 minutes.
web.help.dashboard.decisions: Valid findings that need your choice, or are too large for one pull request, gathered in one GitHub issue per audit. Close the issue as completed once you have dealt with them, or as not planned to drop them: lastcall marks them resolved or dismissed.
web.help.dashboard.plans: Improvements lastcall checked against your code, as checkboxes in a GitHub issue. Tick the ones you want: the next run on that project builds each as a pull request. Closing the issue as completed drops the ideas you did not tick; closing it as not planned drops the ticked ones not built yet too.
web.help.dashboard.state: State: only active projects get bursts. The priority multiplies a project's points when lastcall picks what to work on next; you change both on the Projects page.
web.help.dashboard.trigger: Trigger: burst, when lastcall started it on its own with leftover quota; manual, when you started it, from the Projects page or the command line. After the dot comes the kind of work, when it is not an audit: improvement, labelled issues, tests or dependencies.
web.help.dashboard.status: Status: stopped early means that before a step the account had reached your reserve or its monthly budget, had paid usage on, or had no quota reading, so the run ended there. Interrupted means lastcall itself stopped while the run was going, for example at a restart. Failed means an error stopped it.
web.help.projects.active: Active projects take part in bursts. Even then, a burst skips a project while it has 2 lastcall pull requests waiting for you, or when the same account audited it in the last 7 days, unless you ticked ideas or labelled issues for it. The run buttons work even when the project is inactive. Click the state at the top of a card to turn bursts on or off; the “Active” box in Settings does the same.
web.help.projects.weight: When an account has quota to spend, lastcall gives each active project points (never audited by that account, days and new commits since its last audit, pending findings, errors in production, what you asked for) and starts with the highest. Priority multiplies those points: High (×2) doubles them, Low (×0.5) halves them. It does not make a run longer.
web.help.projects.language: The language of this project's pull requests, issues and reports. With “The account's”, lastcall writes in the language of whichever account does the run, set on the Accounts page. It does not change these pages or your notifications.
web.help.projects.max_prs: The most pull requests one run opens on this project, whatever it does: an audit, tests, dependency upgrades, the ideas of a plan or labelled issues. What does not fit waits for a later run.
web.help.projects.merge_on_approve: On GitHub, approving a pull request does not merge it. With this on, lastcall merges its own pull requests (never a revert) once someone who can write to the repository approves the latest commit, nobody with write access asks for changes, and no check fails or is still running. If one no longer merges cleanly, lastcall closes it and a later run makes the change again on the current code.
web.help.projects.watch: For a day after one of lastcall's pull requests is merged, lastcall watches the checks of the merged commit and the health address below. If the checks fail where they passed before, or the address fails 3 times in a row, it opens a pull request that reverts the change, pauses the project (unticks “Active”) and tells you. It never merges the revert: you decide.
web.help.projects.health_url: Used only while “Watch after the merge” is on and a merge is being watched. lastcall asks it every 10 minutes; any answer with a status from 200 to 399 within 10 seconds counts as working.
web.help.projects.turns: Bursts on this project take turns: an audit, then tests, then dependency upgrades (each only if ticked), then an audit again. Tests too adds tests for behavior no test checks. Dependencies too upgrades what needs more than a new version number: known vulnerabilities, deprecated packages, major versions behind. Ideas you ticked in a plan and issues labelled lastcall always go first.
web.help.projects.signals: Its short name in the tracker's URLs. lastcall reads this project's unresolved errors with a read-only token: a project with errors in the last day ranks higher, and its audits see the error's type, its message with personal data masked, and the lines of your own code. Request data, user data and local variables never reach a model.
web.help.projects.account: Any free account takes the account that is not running anything and has the most quota left before its reset. Choose an account to use that one.
web.help.projects.account_all: With the option for all free accounts, every free account reviews the project and the one with the most quota left judges the findings and writes the fixes. Only an audit can use them all: for Improve now, tests and upgrades it means any free account.
web.help.projects.run_now: These start a run right away, even while bursts are paused or the project is inactive: on the account you choose (waiting until it is free) or, with “Any free account”, on the free account with the most quota left. A project holds one waiting order at a time: clicking again while one waits adds nothing.
web.help.projects.improve: The first run opens an issue with a checkbox per idea that lastcall checked against your code. Tick the ones you want: the next run on this project builds them, one pull request each. While a plan still has ideas to tick, a new plan waits.
web.help.projects.tickets: Open GitHub issues with the label lastcall, which lastcall adds to the repository of each active project. A burst on this project works on them before anything else, the oldest first: a pull request that closes each one, or a comment that says why not. Label an issue yourself to give lastcall work.
web.help.projects.score: lastcall scores each repository without calling any model: recent activity, tests, CI, a setup where it can check its fixes, and open issues. Very large or tiny repositories lose points, and archived, forked or empty ones are left out. It recommends those with 40 points or more.
web.help.projects.size: How much code lastcall would read, at about 4 characters per token. Above 400k tokens, an audit covers only part of the code.
web.help.projects.refresh: lastcall reads your repositories again by itself every 6 hours; the button does it now. The “N more repositories” list holds those under 40 points and those left out because they are archived, forks or empty.
web.help.projects.install: lastcall only sees the repositories where its GitHub App is installed. This link opens GitHub, where you add or remove them; then read again from GitHub here.
web.help.accounts.kind: A subscription spends quota you already pay for, before it resets. An API key is billed per use, so lastcall keeps to a monthly budget you set. A local model runs on this machine and costs nothing, but it needs a strong computer: the suggested one is about 19 GB.
web.help.accounts.enabled: Untick it and lastcall leaves this account alone: it stops reading its quota, starts no bursts on it and does not use it for the runs you start either. Its sign-in and settings stay.
web.help.accounts.policy.before-reset: What is left before each reset: lastcall works on its own only in the hours before the weekly window resets, and only with what would be lost above your reserve.
web.help.accounts.policy.budget: Its budget, at the pace of the month: lastcall works while less of the budget is spent than of the month has gone, so by the 10th it has used about a third.
web.help.accounts.policy.schedule: At the hours of its schedule: lastcall works only inside the hours of its cron schedule, in UTC. An account on an API key still stops at its monthly budget.
web.help.accounts.policy.manual: Only the runs you start: lastcall never starts anything on this account by itself; you start runs from the Projects page.
web.help.accounts.language: The language lastcall writes this account's pull requests, issues and reports in, unless a project sets its own. It does not change these pages or your notifications.
web.help.accounts.login: It opens the tool's own sign-in and keeps the session in a Docker volume for this account only, named lastcall-account- followed by the account's name; lastcall never sees your credentials. Use the second line in Windows PowerShell.
web.help.accounts.check: Takes one reading now, in the sandbox and without calling any model, to check that the sign-in works. It runs in the background: reload the page after a minute.
web.help.accounts.effort: How long the model thinks before it answers. More effort usually finds more and spends more quota or budget. Default keeps lastcall's choice for this level, shown in brackets, and lastcall updates it when its catalogs change.
web.help.accounts.tiers: Each step of a run asks for a level. Balanced runs the reviewers: bugs, security, hygiene, performance, tests and dependencies. Deep runs the judge, the code that writes each fix, and the improvement plans. No built-in step uses Fast: only your repository's own reviewers in .lastcall/reviewers/ that ask for it.
web.help.accounts.engine_field: The subscription and the official tool lastcall runs with it. It must be a subscription that signs in with its own login: an API key goes in the API key option.
web.help.accounts.id: It names the account on its card, in its sign-in command, in the logs and in its Docker volume. It cannot be changed later.
web.help.accounts.review_model: It becomes the model of the Fast and Balanced levels, so all the reviewers use it: bugs, security, hygiene, performance, tests and dependencies. The judge and the fixes keep the main model. You can change both later in Models and effort.
web.help.settings.language: Saved in this browser for a year. Until you choose, lastcall follows your browser's language. Your notifications have their own language, under Notifications, and what lastcall writes on GitHub follows each account and project.
web.help.settings.notify_language: The language of the messages lastcall sends you, whatever language these pages show. Until you save one, lastcall takes the language of these pages when you add your first destination.
web.help.settings.signals_project: In Sentry and GlitchTip, each app sends its errors to a project with a short name in its URLs. Give that name to a lastcall project on the Projects page: its audits then read its unresolved errors of the last 14 days, the most frequent first.
web.help.settings.logs_project: Type to narrow the list, which holds the repositories on your Projects page: write one as that page does, in any case. Anything else is refused. lastcall reads the logs of a container, or of a source, only once you give it a project.
web.help.settings.logs_suggested: lastcall pairs a container, or a source in Loki, with one of your projects from its image, its Compose project or its name, when only one project fits. It reads nothing until you read it here. Skipping a suggestion records your no, so that it does not come back; you can still give it a project below, among the others.
web.help.settings.loki_label: Loki tags each stream of logs with labels. lastcall lists the values of one label as sources, one per app or container, seen in the last 7 days. It uses the first that your Loki has of container, container_name, service_name, app and job. Choose another only if your apps go by a different label: your project choices then start over.
web.help.settings.loki_sources: The names next to each source are the machines where it ran, from the host label of its logs. The Compose project, when Loki has it, is one of the clues lastcall uses to propose a project; it reads nothing until you choose one.
web.help.settings.loki_tenant: Leave it empty unless your Loki keeps the logs of several teams apart (multi-tenant) and its admin gave you a tenant name. lastcall sends it in the X-Scope-OrgID header of every request.
web.help.settings.loki_token: With a user, lastcall signs in with that user and this password (basic login). Without a user, it sends this as a bearer token, the way a token-protected Loki or proxy expects.
web.help.settings.destination: Each line is the destination as Apprise, the library that sends lastcall's notifications, writes it, with its secrets hidden. The full address stays in lastcall's secret store.
web.help.settings.save_test: lastcall sends the test first and saves the destination only if it gets through. If it fails, you see what the service answered, and nothing is saved.
web.help.settings.find_chat: lastcall asks Telegram for the chats that wrote to your bot lately and lists them, so you need not look up your chat ID. It only reads: nothing is sent or saved yet.
web.help.settings.event.decisions: After an audit, the findings that need your choice go into one GitHub issue per run. You get one message with how many there are and a link to the issue. It also covers improvement plans: when a plan opens, one message with the number of ideas to choose from and a link to its issue.
web.help.settings.event.merged: Only for projects with “Merge after my approval” on, on the Projects page: when you approve one of lastcall's pull requests on GitHub, lastcall merges it and tells you.
web.help.settings.event.reverted: Only for projects with “Watch after the merge” on: when a merged lastcall change breaks the checks or the health address within a day, lastcall opens a pull request that reverts it, pauses the project and tells you. You decide whether to merge it.
web.help.settings.event.paid: When an account turns on extra paid usage, credits or overage billing, lastcall spends nothing from it until that is off. You hear it once, when it starts.
web.help.settings.event.quota: lastcall reads each account's quota every 15 minutes. While a reading fails, for example because the sign-in expired, that account spends nothing. You hear it once, when it starts failing.
web.help.settings.event.burst: Off by default. When on, you hear each time an account starts a burst: what is left and the time to its reset, or its budget or its schedule.
web.help.github.app: A GitHub App is a bot identity that you own. lastcall acts as it with the App's private key, which GitHub hands over once and lastcall keeps in its secret store. It never asks for your GitHub password or tokens.
web.help.github.owner: The App has to belong to the account that owns the repositories lastcall will work on, because a private App can only be installed there: your own username, or the organization that holds them. Type just the name, as in github.com/name. lastcall asks GitHub, with no credentials, whether it is a person or an organization. The App will be called lastcall- followed by the name, cut to 34 characters.
web.help.github.permissions: contents lets lastcall push its own branches, pull requests lets it open them, and issues lets it open the issues with decisions and ideas, and label issues. checks and statuses, read only, let it see whether the checks of a commit pass, for “Merge after my approval” and “Watch after the merge”. metadata: read is the basic access every App has. With no webhooks, GitHub never calls lastcall, so it needs no public address.
web.help.github.create: GitHub opens so you can confirm, then sends you back here. This button works once and for one hour; after that, start again from Continue.
web.help.github.install: Creating the App gives it no repositories yet. Installing does: lastcall can only see and change the repositories you choose, and they appear on the Projects page. Open this link again at any time to change them.
web.help.setup.code: lastcall writes it to its log when it starts, and again after a password reset, on a line like Web UI setup code: ABCD-EFGH. Capitals and the dash do not matter. If lastcall has restarted since, use the newest code in the log.
web.help.setup.why: Without it, anyone who can open this page could choose the password. Only someone who can read the server's log sees the code, and it works only once.
web.help.setup.password: lastcall has one password, for its owner, and no user names. It keeps only an scrypt hash of it in its secret store. At most 256 characters.
web.help.login.session: This browser stays signed in for 30 days, or until 7 days pass without use. Sign out ends the session in this browser only; a password reset ends them all.
web.help.login.reset: The command deletes only the password and signs out every browser. Your projects, accounts and settings stay. Then this page asks for a new setup code from the log.
web.help.login.locked: Wrong passwords and wrong setup codes both count. Five from your address within 15 minutes, or 20 from anywhere, pause attempts until 15 minutes after the last failure.
web.help.error.origin: lastcall accepts forms only from the address it is served at. Behind a reverse proxy, set LASTCALL_TRUST_PROXY=1, or LASTCALL_WEB_ORIGIN to its public address such as https://lastcall.example.com, in the .env file, then run docker compose up -d again.
web.help.error.csrf: Each form carries a code tied to the sign-in that showed it. If you signed out and in again after opening the page, reload it to get the current code.
web.help.accounts.policy.title: When it spends
web.login.welcome: Welcome back. Your leftover quota is in good hands.
web.plan.held.paused: Bursts are paused: this account spends no leftover quota on its own until you resume them. Runs you start from Projects still run.
web.plan.held.paused_working: Bursts are paused: the run under way finishes, then this account spends no leftover quota on its own until you resume them. Runs you start from Projects still run.
web.plan.held.down: The service has stopped: nothing bursts until it starts again.
web.project.legend.writes: What it writes and may do
web.project.active_hint: Bursts may pick it. The run buttons work either way.
web.project.merge_hint: lastcall merges its own pull requests once they are approved and their checks pass.
web.project.watch_hint: For a day after a merge, if the checks or the health address break, lastcall proposes a revert and pauses the project.
web.project.checks.lead: “{merge}” and “{watch}” need the GitHub App to read checks and commit statuses, and this App cannot yet.
web.project.checks.open: Open the App's permissions on GitHub.
web.project.checks.set: Set “Checks” and “Commit statuses” to “Read-only” and save.
web.project.checks.accept: Accept the new permissions where GitHub asks for it, on the App's installation: Settings › Applications › Installed GitHub Apps › Configure, or the organization's settings.
web.project.tests_turn: In turn with the audits, it adds tests for behavior that no test checks.
web.project.deps_turn: In turn with the audits, it upgrades what needs more than a new version number.
web.settings.events_hint: They apply once you add a destination above.
web.setup.step1_text: lastcall writes a setup code in its log. Show the log with:
web.project.remove_stops: lastcall stops working on this repository.
web.project.remove_history: Its history and what lastcall learned stay. Add it again and it picks up where it left off, without proposing again what you rejected.
web.project.remove_settings: Its settings (priority, language and the rest) are forgotten.
web.project.remove_github: Nothing changes on GitHub: the repository and its pull requests stay.
web.project.remove_back: It goes back to the list of repositories to add.
web.project.remove_busy: A run is going on {repo} right now. Remove it when the run ends.
web.done.removed: {repo} removed. Its history stays: add it again from the list below at any time.
web.logs.gone: It was chosen for {project}, which is not a project now: add {project} again and it is read again.
